messages.subject: knitr and German characters
parts:
Hi,

I am working on an .Rnw document with my MacBook Pro. When I compile with texshop I get the table though some German words with special Characters like äöü are not correctly represented... instead the characters are simply left out. 

I am using \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} and also tried e.g. 'Deutsche B\"orse', 'Deutsche B\\"orse' or 'Deutsche B\"{o}rse', though nothing works.

messages.author: e7658bf6e6befd70
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and German characters
parts:
The key is to know the character encoding of your Rnw file, and you
have to pass that encoding to knitr::knit(). If it is really UTF8
encoded, you may call

library(knitr)
knit('input.Rnw', encoding='UTF-8')

And you have to use \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} in the LaTeX preamble.
Then you compile input.tex with whatever LaTeX tools you want. You did
not send an example, so it is impossible to know what was going on.
Your actual encoding might be iso-8859-15, in which case you use
\usepackage[latin9]{inputenc} and knit('input.Rnw',
encoding='iso-8859-15').

I recommend you to try RStudio instead, which handles encoding
automatically so you do not need to type all these knit() commands.
However, you still need to be aware of the encoding, since you have to
decide \usepackage[???]{inputenc}.

Regards,
Yihui
